prompts: Pixel Arena, our Unreal game in {WS}, runs fine in the editor. In the packaged build, players say the arena has no colors, and the game crashes after a minute or so of play. The log of one packaged run is in {WS}/Saved/Logs. There is no engine on this machine, so you cannot build or run it. Find out why and fix the sources and the config. Record the causes in {WS}/result.json: crash_cause, no_colors_cause.
answers:
**[goal]** Find and fix why the packaged Pixel Arena build has no colors and crashes after ~1 minute; record causes in `result.json`.

**[action]** Read the shipping log, config, and source; applied three fixes; wrote `result.json`.

**[result]**

**No colors** — the palette asset was never cooked into the package. `DefaultGame.ini` had `bCookAll=False` and only `/Game/Data/Effects` in `DirectoriesToAlwaysCook`, so `LoadObject<UArenaPalette>("/Game/Data/Palettes/DA_Primary")` in `BeginPlay` failed. Log evidence: `Couldn't find file for package /Game/Data/Palettes/DA_Primary` and `Palette is null, using fallback gray`. Fix: added `+DirectoriesToAlwaysCook=(Path="/Game/Data/Palettes")` to `Config/DefaultGame.ini`.

**Crash** — null/dangling pointer deref of `ScoreTracker` in `OnGoalScored` → `UArenaScoreTracker::AddPoints` (`ArenaScoreTracker.cpp:18`, `EXCEPTION_ACCESS_VIOLATION`). `ScoreTracker` was a plain C++ pointer, not a `UPROPERTY`, so the GC could collect the `UArenaScoreTracker` created in `BeginPlay`; the log shows `Collecting garbage: 412 objects purged` at ~1 min, and the crash fires on the first goal right after. Fix: made it `UPROPERTY() TObjectPtr<UArenaScoreTracker>` (GC-protected, matching `Hud`/`Palette`) and added a null guard in `OnGoalScored` as defense in depth.

**[evidence]** Log lines 4–6 (palette), 8 (GC), 10–14 (crash stack naming `AddPoints` and `OnGoalScored`); all three edited files re-read and verified above; `result.json` written with `crash_cause` and `no_colors_cause`.

**[assumptions/limits]** `ArenaScoreTracker.cpp` isn't in this workspace, so the fix targets the visible root cause (untracked pointer) rather than editing that file; no build/run possible here (no engine), so fixes are verified by code/log correlation only. No browser tabs or windows were opened, so nothing to close.
